items.title: Blast at explosives storage site kills dozens in Myanmar

featured_image.name: Blast kills dozens in village in rebel-held region of Myanmar

items.description: An explosion at a building storing mining explosives in northeastern Myanmar killed at least 46 people on Sunday, including six children, with local media reporting death tolls as high as 55. About 70 others were injured in the blast, which struck around noon in the village of Kaungtup in Namhkam township, roughly two miles from the Chinese border.

items.title: Lula rejects U.S. terrorist label for Brazil's largest gangs

featured_image.name: Lula blasts US for labelling Brazil crime factions as terrorists

items.description:
Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva on Friday denounced the United States' decision to designate two of Brazil's largest criminal organizations as terrorist groups, calling it undue interference in the country's internal affairs and warning Washington against treating Brazil "like a banana republic."

"We will not accept being treated like children, we will not accept being treated as if we were a banana republic," Lula said at a public event on Friday, referring to "a certain Marco Rubio, who said that our criminals are terrorists and that Americans can intervene".[1][2]

items.title: Philippines says China threat persists despite Trump-Xi summit

featured_image.name: Philippines defence chief Gilberto Teodoro Jr calls out China's 'propaganda  spiel' at Shangri-La Dialogue | The Straits Times

items.description: The Philippines' defense secretary Gilberto Teodoro Jr. said on Saturday that the country remains under "severe threat" from China, declaring that a recent thaw in U.S.-China relations following the Trump-Xi summit in Beijing has done nothing to ease tensions in the South China Sea.[1][2]

items.title: Quarter of trapped oil tankers slip out of Hormuz

featured_image.name: A Quarter of Large Oil Tankers Trapped by Iran War Have ...

items.description: A slow, stealthy trickle of oil tankers has begun slipping out of the Persian Gulf through the Strait of Hormuz, with roughly one-quarter of the large non-Iranian vessels stranded since the war began now having crossed the chokepoint, even as Chevron CEO Mike Wirth warned that ships continue to come under attack.

items.title: Ebola funding pledges nearly halved as outbreak spreads

featured_image.name: Ebola outbreak: What travel restrictions have countries ...

items.description:
International financial commitments to combat the Ebola outbreak in Central and East Africa have nearly halved in a matter of days, Africa CDC Director-General Jean Kaseya revealed Thursday, as the deadly Bundibugyo strain continues to spread through the Democratic Republic of Congo and Uganda with no approved vaccine available.

Speaking from Kinshasa, Kaseya said pledges that stood at nearly $500 million on Monday, May 25, had dropped to approximately $290 million by Thursday after multiple donors withdrew their commitments. The collapse in funding represents a loss of roughly $210 million at a moment when the outbreak has grown to more than 1,000 suspected cases and 246 deaths in the DRC alone.[1][2][3]

items.title: Rubio thanks Pakistan for Iran mediation efforts

featured_image.name: US-PAKISTAN-DIPLOMACY

items.description: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio met with Pakistani Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar at the State Department on Friday, with discussions centering on Pakistan's role mediating the ongoing U.S.-Iran conflict and the broader bilateral relationship between Washington and Islamabad.[1][2][3]

items.title: Trump's Situation Room meeting on Iran ends without deal

featured_image.name: Trump enters Situation Room to make 'final determination' on Iran

items.description:
President Donald Trump convened a high-stakes meeting in the White House Situation Room on Friday to make what he called a "final determination" on a proposed memorandum of understanding with Iran, but the nearly two-hour session ended without a resolution, according to The New York Times.[1]

The meeting came after Trump announced his plans in a Truth Social post Friday morning, writing, "I will be meeting now, in the Situation Room, to make a final determination". He outlined preconditions for any agreement, insisting that Iran "must agree that they will never have a Nuclear Weapon or Bomb" and that the Strait of Hormuz must "immediately open" to unrestricted shipping with no tolls.[2][3][4][5]

items.title: Chevron CEO says ships attacked in Strait of Hormuz this week

featured_image.name: Chevron CEO says Iran war impact isn't fully priced into oil ...

items.description: Chevron CEO Mike Wirth disclosed in an interview with Bloomberg TV that multiple vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz were attacked this week, including incidents not yet publicly reported, even as ceasefire optimism between the United States and Iran drove oil prices sharply lower.[1][2]

items.title: Trump announces lifting of naval blockade on Iran

featured_image.name: What we know about the US military's blockade of Iran

items.description: President Trump declared on Friday that the U.S. naval blockade of the Strait of Hormuz "will now be lifted," posting the announcement on Truth Social after convening in the White House Situation Room to make what officials described as a "final determination" on the deal with Iran. The announcement follows weeks of fraught negotiations and marks the most concrete step toward ending the nearly three-month conflict between the United States and Iran.[1][2]

items.title: China building 80-plus launch pads near nuclear silos

featured_image.name: China's Nuclear Acceleration Revealed in Satellite Images

items.description:
China is constructing a sprawling network of launch pads, bunkers, and communications nodes near its nuclear missile silos in the remote deserts of its northwest, according to a Reuters analysis of satellite imagery published on Friday.[1][2]

The images reveal more than 80 pads that could be used by China's expanding fleet of mobile missile launchers and air-defense batteries, along with facilities that may support electronic warfare, satellite communication, and command operations, according to three security experts who reviewed the imagery for Reuters.[2]

items.title: US-Iran draft deal includes $300B reconstruction fund for Tehran

featured_image.name: In razing its modernist buildings, Iran is erasing its past Western  influence

items.description: A draft memorandum of understanding between the United States and Iran contains a proposed $300 billion reconstruction and investment program for Tehran, according to an Iranian lawmaker and reporting from The New York Times, adding a striking economic dimension to the emerging framework aimed at ending the three-month-old war.

items.title: Suspected Russian drone strikes building in Romania, injuring two

featured_image.name: In Romania, a drone crashed into a high-rise building; a fire broke out  following an explosion | УНН

items.description:
A suspected Russian attack drone struck a residential apartment building in the Romanian border city of Galati early on May 29, causing an explosion and injuring at least two people, according to Romanian media reports and social media accounts from the scene.[1][2]

The incident occurred during an overnight Russian drone assault targeting Ukraine's Odesa region, which shares a border with Romania's Galati county. Romanian news outlet MediaFax reported that the drone impacted the building, with two people sustaining injuries. Fighter jets were scrambled in response, and Romanian authorities dispatched forensic teams and explosives experts to investigate.[2][1]

items.title: Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket explodes during test at Cape Canaveral

featured_image.name: Blue Origin rocket explodes during an engine-firing test

items.description:
A Blue Origin New Glenn rocket exploded during an engine-firing test at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station on Thursday evening, sending a fireball into the night sky and rattling homes across the surrounding area. No injuries were reported.

The explosion occurred around 9 p.m. at Launch Complex 36, where residents of Cape Canaveral and Cocoa Beach felt tremors and soon flooded social media with images of the blast. Blue Origin confirmed the incident in a brief statement: "We encountered an anomaly during today's hotfire test. We will share updates as we gather more information."[1]

Jeff Bezos responded on X, writing: "It's too early to determine the underlying cause, but we are already investigating. Today has been challenging, but we will reconstruct whatever needs to be rebuilt and resume our flights. It's worth the effort."[1]

items.title: Hungary's Magyar vows 'reliable' NATO role but won't arm Ukraine

featured_image.name: NATO Secretary General meets with the Prime Minister of Hungary | NATO  Photo gallery

items.description: NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte met with Hungarian Prime Minister Péter Magyar in Brussels on Thursday to discuss preparations for the alliance's upcoming summit in Ankara, as Budapest seeks to rebuild its standing within the transatlantic alliance while maintaining its refusal to arm Ukraine.

items.title: US denies Iran's claim it destroyed American aircraft in Bushehr

featured_image.name: Iran accuses US of ceasefire violation

items.description: Iran's state television reported early Friday that a US aircraft was destroyed in the Jam governorate of Bushehr province in southern Iran, citing local governor Masoud Tangestani. A US official denied the claim to Reuters, stating no American aircraft had been shot down near Bushehr, and no independent confirmation of the Iranian report has emerged.[1][2][3]

items.title: Vance says US and Iran 'very close' to ceasefire deal

featured_image.name: US, Iran "very close" to deal to end war, Vance says

items.description:
Vice President JD Vance told reporters on Thursday that the United States and Iran are "very close" to finalizing a memorandum of understanding that would extend their ceasefire for 60 days, reopen the Strait of Hormuz, and restart nuclear discussions — but cautioned the two sides are "not there yet."

The remarks came as Axios reported that US and Iranian negotiators have reached consensus on the terms of the MOU, though the agreement remains unsigned pending approval from President Trump and Iran's supreme leadership. Trump has been briefed on the proposal but has requested "a couple of days" to deliberate before giving his final endorsement.[1][2]

items.title: Japan calls Russian criticism of its military buildup 'ridiculous' at UN

featured_image.name: Japan dismisses 'ridiculous' Russian criticism of military buildup | Reuters

items.description: Japan's UN ambassador on Thursday rejected Russia's criticism of Japan's defense expansion as "ridiculous," pushing back against Moscow's accusations during a UN Security Council open debate on upholding the principles of the UN Charter.

items.title: US to designate Brazil's two largest gangs as terrorist organizations

featured_image.name: Death toll in Brazil police raid on drug gang in Rio rises

items.description:
The United States announced Thursday that it will classify Brazil's two largest criminal organizations — the Primeiro Comando da Capital (PCC) and the Comando Vermelho (Red Command) — as Foreign Terrorist Organizations, a move that carries sweeping financial and legal consequences and is expected to deepen friction between Washington and Brasília.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio said in a statement that the formal FTO designation will take effect on June 5. In the meantime, the State Department has already classified both gangs as "Specially Designated Global Terrorists," immediately subjecting them to U.S. sanctions.[1][2][3]

items.title: Anthropic raises $65B at $965B valuation, topping OpenAI

featured_image.name: Anthropic set to hit $10.9 billion in revenue in Q2, source ...

items.description:
Anthropic has closed a $65 billion Series H funding round at a post-money valuation of $965 billion, making it the most valuable AI startup in the world and surpassing rival OpenAI, Bloomberg reported on Thursday.[1]

The round was co-led by Altimeter Capital, Dragoneer, Greenoaks, and Sequoia Capital, with additional participation from Capital Group, Coatue, and D1 Capital Partners. The deal caps a whirlwind fundraising process that began in late April, when Anthropic first signaled to investors it was targeting a valuation above $900 billion.[2][3][4][1]

items.title: US and Iran reportedly reach 60-day MOU deal awaiting Trump's approval

featured_image.name: What's inside the Iran deal Trump is close to signing

items.description:
Negotiators from the United States and Iran have reached an agreement on a 60-day memorandum of understanding to extend their ceasefire and begin negotiations over Iran's nuclear program, but President Donald Trump still needs to give final approval, Axios reported on Thursday, citing two U.S. officials.[1]

The reported breakthrough came on a day of renewed violence. Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said it struck a U.S. airbase early Thursday in retaliation for American strikes near the port city of Bandar Abbas, where U.S. forces had intercepted four Iranian attack drones and hit a ground-control station threatening commercial shipping near the Strait of Hormuz.[2][3][4]
